response.answer: Emerging trends in engineering and computer science include scalable optimization methods, interpretable models, and practical extensions for supervised learning. Choquet-integral aggregation and deep learning in smart grid technology are also notable innovations. These advancements aim to improve efficiency, transparency, and application of machine learning models.

The mathemat-ical depth is reinforced by a comprehensive exploration of optimization techniques, covering stochastic gradient descent (SGD), adaptive moment estimation (Adam), and spectral-based regularization methods. Functional approximation is one of the fundamental concepts in deep learning, and it is integral to how deep learning models, particularly neural networks, solve complex prob-lems. results.title: Emerging Trends in Deep Learning for Credit Scoring
results.content: This review paper also explains how tabular datasets are converted into images for the application of a two-dimensional convolutional neural network (CNN) and how “black box” models using local and global rule extraction and rule-based methods are applied in credit scoring. Further, the improvements in accuracy and AUC values achieved with these datasets using ensemble classifiers and their hybrids, DL techniques, rule extraction, and rule-based classifiers for credit scoring have been tabulated as well. The objectives of this review are fourfold: (1) to present certain theoretical characteristics of DBNs and the reasons they achieve higher accuracy than shallower networks with one hidden layer by using ML theorems; (2) to review the most recent DL techniques that have been shown to achieve higher accuracies than ensemble classifiers, their hybrids, rule extraction methods, and rule-based classifiers; (3) to reveal the potential classification capabilities of DL-based classifiers and investigate their applicability to credit scoring datasets; and (4) to provide deep insights into the usefulness and interpretability of DL in credit scoring and related financial areas.
